weaknesses: The abstract inaccurately describes the contributions of the paper, focusing on CRISPR-Cas9 instead of the proposed Incremental Randomized Smoothing framework.
The claims regarding the novelty of IRS are overstated, as incremental approaches have been explored in other contexts without proper acknowledgment.
The limitations of the IRS framework are not sufficiently discussed, particularly regarding its performance with varying levels of noise and different architectures.
strengths: The paper presents a novel framework for incremental certification that has the potential to significantly reduce computational costs in DNN robustness verification.
Empirical results demonstrate substantial speedups in certification times, providing strong evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed method.
The methodology is well-structured, and the insights into the disparity between approximated networks are valuable for future research.
